title: Practice: conditions, loops & nested-loop patterns
overview: This practice day mixes if-else ladders, loops, a little maths (digits, divisors, wrap-around with `%`) and nested loops that draw number, letter and star patterns. For every pattern, the key skill is working out how many items row `i` needs.

concepts.explain: For a two-digit `n`, `n / 10` is the tens digit and `n % 10` is the units digit.
`(ch - 'a' + 1) % 26 + 'a'` moves one letter forward, and 'z' wraps back to 'a'.
`i` divides `n` when `n % i == 0`. Checking every `i` from 1 to n lists all divisors.
Start with `flag = false` and set it to `true` when something happens. After the loop, the flag tells you whether it ever happened.
The outer loop picks the row and the inner loop prints that row's items. Write the item count as a formula in `i`, such as `i`, `n-i+1` or `2*i-1`.
`'A' + i - 1` gives the i-th capital letter.

files.title: Next Alphabet
files.what: Prints the letter after the given lowercase letter, wrapping 'z' around to 'a'.
steps: Read `ch`.
`ch - 'a'` turns the letter into a position from 0 to 25.
Add 1, take `% 26` so that 26 wraps to 0, then add `'a'` to get a letter back.
Print it with `%c`.
files.output_note: For `z` the output is `a`: (25 + 1) % 26 = 0, which is 'a'.

check.q: What does the formula give for 'm'?

files.title: Lucky Numbers (two digits)
files.what: Splits a two-digit number into its digits and says `YES` if one digit divides the other.
steps: `first = n / 10` and `second = n % 10`.
If `first % second == 0` or `second % first == 0`, print `YES`.
Otherwise print `NO`.
files.watch_out: For numbers like 10, 20 or 30, `second` is 0, and `first % second` divides by zero, which crashes the program. Fix: check `second == 0 ||` first. Since 0 is divisible by any digit, those numbers are lucky.

check.a: `n` is between 10 and 99, so its tens digit is at least 1.

files.title: Ali Baba and Puzzles

problem.name: Codeforces group - Ali Baba and Puzzles

files.what: Checks whether some choice of two operators from `+ - *`, placed as `a ? b ? c`, gives `d`. C's usual precedence applies: `*` is done first.
steps: Read `a, b, c, d` as `long long`, since products can be large.
Test each combination with `||`: `a+b+c`, `a+b-c`, `a+b*c`, `a-b+c`, and so on.
Print `YES` if any combination equals `d`, otherwise `NO`.
files.input_note: Four integers a b c d.
files.watch_out: `a - b * c` is listed twice and `a * b * c` is missing, so an input like `2 3 4 24` wrongly prints NO. Fix: replace the repeated check with `a * b * c == d`.

check.q: How many operator combinations are there for two slots with three operators?

files.title: Even Numbers from 1 to N
files.what: Prints every even number from 1 to N, or `-1` if there are none.
steps: Start with `flag = false`.
Loop `i` from 1 to n. When `i % 2 == 0`, print `i` and set `flag = true`.
After the loop, if `flag` is still false, print `-1`.
files.output_note: The output is `2`, `4`, `6`, `8`, one per line. For n = 1, it would print `-1` instead.

check.q: How could you loop over only the even numbers?

files.title: Divisors
files.what: Prints every divisor of n in increasing order by testing each number from 1 to n.
steps: Read `n`.
For `i` from 1 to n, if `n % i == 0`, print `i`.
files.output_note: The divisors of 12 are listed in order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

check.q: Name a faster way to find divisors.
check.a: Only check `i` up to √n. Each divisor `i` you find gives a second one, `n / i`.

files.title: Pattern: 1 / 1 2 / 1 2 3 ...
steps: The outer loop runs `i` from 1 to n.
The inner loop runs `j` from 1 to i and prints `j `.
A newline ends each row.
files.output_note: There are 4 rows, and each is one number longer than the row above.

check.q: How many numbers are printed in total for n = 4?

files.title: Pattern: counting down rows
files.what: Row `i` counts down from `i` to 1, and `i` itself goes down from n to 1.
steps: The outer loop runs `i` from n down to 1.
The inner loop runs `j` from i down to 1 and prints `j `.
A newline ends each row.

check.q: What changes if the inner loop runs from 1 up to i instead?
check.a: Each row counts up (`1 2 3 4`, then `1 2 3`, and so on), and the rows still get shorter.

files.title: Pattern: A / B B / C C C
files.what: Row `i` prints the i-th letter `i` times.
steps: The outer loop runs `i` from 1 to n.
The inner loop prints `'A' + i - 1` exactly `i` times, using `%c`.
files.output_note: The output is `A`, `B B`, `C C C`, `D D D D`.

files.title: Pattern: star pyramid
files.what: A centred pyramid. Row `i` has `2*(n-i)` leading spaces and then `2*i-1` stars, each star followed by a space.
steps: The outer loop runs `i` from 1 to n.
Print `2*(n-i)` spaces. The count is doubled because every star takes two characters (`* `).
Print `2*i-1` copies of `* `.
End the row with a newline.
files.output_note: The rows have 1, 3, 5 and 7 stars and are centred. The top row starts after 6 spaces.

check.q: How many stars are on the last row for n = 10?

recap: Use `/ 10` and `% 10` to split off digits.
Use `% 26` to wrap around the alphabet.
A flag remembers whether something happened inside a loop.
For patterns, write each row's space and item counts as formulas in `i`.
Never use `%` with a value that might be 0.

check_yourself.q: Which loops print this pattern for n=3: `***`, `**`, `*`?
check_yourself.a: `for (i = n; i >= 1; i--) { for (j = 1; j <= i; j++) printf("*"); printf("\n"); }`

check_yourself.q: What is `(24 + 3) % 26`, and what does it mean for letters?
Why does pattern4 print `2*(n-i)` spaces instead of `n-i`?
check_yourself.a: Each star is printed as two characters (`* `), so the gap has to be twice as wide to keep the pyramid centred.
